description: Content-scoped contract bits moved OUT of base.contract.json by the Swift 2.4 base split (base 3.0.0 framework-only). surface-swift owns the Swift content surface: the Swift 2 content area (area 3, EN), the entire merge tree, UrlPath, and its own item-type XMLs (itemtypes/, from the official Swift v2.4.0 design package) so the surface is self-contained.

urlPathOwnership.decision: UrlPath ships in surface-swift (replace/_sql/UrlPath), NOT in base 3.0.0.
urlPathOwnership.rationale: The table's single row is a 301 friendly-URL redirect (products-* -> Default.aspx?ID=50) bound to UrlPathAreaId 3 and a Swift page id. Friendly URLs resolve against pages; a framework-only base ships no areas and no pages, so a base-owned UrlPath row would dangle and force base re-proves on Swift page churn. It travels with the content it routes.

navDepth.note: Menu-bar affordance obligation (RUN-NAV-DEFAULT): the header nav needs >=1 menu-visible child relation for the theme affordance probes to exercise dropdown depth. Owned by the Swift content tree (surface-swift); the gate's Ensure-NavDepth authors the minimal depth when absent.

titleRules.note: Title-integrity contract (gate Step 10c2): for every item-typed page, DB item Title == YAML fields.Title. Applies to this surface's replace/_content tree.

perEnvironmentAreaExclusions.note: Per-environment Area configuration deliberately NOT serialized by the base (LRN-08). These Area columns/fields are excluded by config/swift-2.3.json (the 'Site framework' deploy predicate's excludeAreaColumns + excludeFields), so the base ships brand/content-neutral structure only and every consuming environment owns these values. A fresh deserialize therefore leaves them at whatever the target DB already holds - it does NOT overwrite them. 1.13.3 narrows the exclusion by exactly ONE column: AreaEcomCurrencyId is no longer per-environment and is now SHIPPED as EUR in both area documents. It names a base-owned constant (EUR is CurrencyIsDefault on every EUR$$<lang> row the base ships), and an unbound area is not neutral: on DW 10.28 it resolves the REQUEST CULTURE's currency, so an /en-us/ storefront serves USD carts and every EUR EcomPrices row - contract, customer-group and quantity-tier - falls through to EcomProducts.ProductPrice (Foundry #1232, measured on foundry-sd4v.mydwsite4.com: cart CART783 OrderCurrencyCode USD, TCPROD0046 45.00 instead of 36.90). The obligation could not be discharged online either: a remote consumer reaching the host by URL and Admin API key has no SQL channel, and /Admin/Api/AreaSave refuses an area whose layoutTemplate is empty ('Default page template: The value is required.'), so a binding the price resolver depends on has to travel with the layer.

consumerObligation.bindSiteRoot: After deserialize, set each area's AreaFrontpage to the environment's site-root page id.
consumerObligation.bindProductPrimaryPage: After deserialize, set SHOP1's ShopProductPrimaryPageId (EcomShops) to the environment's product detail page id (the Shop/Product Details page this layer ships). The base ships it as 0 because page ids are allocated per environment; until it is set, a product URL generated outside a page context has no primary page to resolve against.
consumerObligation.restart: Restart the DW host after binding - Area routing, frontpage resolution, and shop resolution are cached at host startup. The same holds for the three columns 1.13.3 now ships: the deserialize writes them, the running application still serves the old binding until it restarts.
consumerObligation.bindCountryAndStockLocation: AreaEcomCountryCode and AreaStockLocationID stay per-environment and are still excluded: they drive VAT and stock resolution against the consumer's own market.

shippedAreaEcomBinding.AreaEcomCurrencyId: EUR - CurrencyIsDefault on every EUR$$<lang> row the base ships. Shipped in BOTH mode trees (replace/_content/Swift 2/area.yml and merge/_content/Swift 2/area.yml). Every EcomPrices row the Distribution ships carries an EMPTY PriceShopId, so the currency is the only area binding price resolution needs.
shippedAreaEcomBinding.consumerOverride: A consumer on a different default currency overrides AreaEcomCurrencyId after deserialize, the same way it binds AreaFrontpage and AreaEcomShopId. The shipped value is the Distribution's own default, not a refusal to be re-pointed.
shippedAreaEcomBinding.knownGap: merge/merge-manifest.json carries no excludeAreaColumns, so the merge pass writes the merge document's AreaEcomShopId and AreaEcomLanguageId. Until 1.13.8 both were EMPTY STRINGS there, so a merge deserialize BLANKED a binding the replace pass or the consumer had set - which is why a delivered swift-demo host served querystring product URLs even with the replace tree correct. 1.13.8 ships SHOP1/ENU in the merge document too, so the two passes agree.
shippedAreaEcomBinding.AreaEcomShopId: SHOP1 - the ONE shop the base ships ('B2B Commerce Store'). Shipped in BOTH mode trees since 1.13.8. It is not cosmetic: the Swift Shop page carries Dynamicweb.Ecommerce.Frontend.UrlHandling.ShopUrlDataProvider with IncludeFrom=ContextShop, so an area with no shop gives the DW10 URL index nothing to index and every product and group link falls back to the querystring form (Foundry #1281, measured on foundry.mydwsite4.com, DW 10.28.10).
shippedAreaEcomBinding.AreaEcomLanguageId: ENU - LanguageIsDefault in EcomLanguages and the IsDefault side of the base-owned EcomShopLanguageRelation SHOP1/ENU row. Shipped in BOTH mode trees since 1.13.8. The same URL provider carries IncludeLanguage=ContextLanguage, so the shop binding ALONE does not produce friendly URLs - both bindings are required. Measured on foundry.mydwsite4.com: shop bound + language empty renders querystring, language bound + shop empty renders querystring, both bound renders /en-us/shop/data-models/bundles-bom/truvio-bundle-kit-41 with a matching PDP canonical (Foundry #1281).
shippedAreaEcomBinding.shopBindingObligesGroupRelations: Binding AreaEcomShopId makes DW enforce group-in-shop on every product page, so EVERY browsable group needs an EcomShopGroupRelation row or its PDP dies with System.NullReferenceException at Dynamicweb.Ecommerce.ProductCatalog.ProductCatalogFrontend.IsGroupInCorrectShop, rendered as a dw-error module block (Foundry #1237, re-measured on foundry.mydwsite4.com 2026-09-17). The relation rows are owned by the layer that owns the groups: sample-data 4.1.3 relates all sixteen TCGRP groups to SHOP1 (it shipped only the four top groups before). The rows do NOT affect the URL shape - dropping the twelve subgroup rows leaves the friendly URLs intact and breaks only the PDP. A consumer shipping its own catalogue layer carries the same obligation.

protectedItemTypes.note: Upstream DW/Swift identifiers - NEVER renamed by the vocabulary rewrite (plan section 3.1). PK tables are ItemType_<systemName> (hyphenated on DW 10.26.9). (Swift list owned by surface-swift since the base split; Headless list owned by surface-headless.)

fieldDisplayGroupsBound.note: The PDP Specifications band (replace/_content/Swift 2/Shop/Product Details/grid-row-13/paragraph-c1-10.yml) binds DisplayGroups ["tc_specs"]. surface-swift NAMES the group; it creates none. These are the guarantees a composing data layer must keep, because the band renders a heading over an empty table when any of them is broken and says nothing about which (Foundry #1147).

obligations.availableInFrontend: EcomFieldDisplayGroups.FieldDisplayGroupAvailableInFrontend = 1. The paragraph's own option query filters on it, so a group without it is invisible to the storefront AND to the backend picker.
obligations.memberReferenceForm: A member of a display group is a REFERENCE to a field, not a field id. A category field is referenced as ProductCategory|<FieldCategoryId>|<FieldId>. A bare FieldId resolves against GLOBAL product fields (EcomProductField) only.
obligations.membershipIsComplete: EcomFieldDisplayGroupFields must hold every field the group claims, and the denormalised EcomFieldDisplayGroups.FieldDisplayGroupFieldIds must be WRITTEN FROM that relation rather than typed beside it. The two stores disagreeing is the measured failure: 28 members in the relation against 6 names in the column.
obligations.everyNameResolves: Every name in FieldDisplayGroupFieldIds must resolve to a live EcomProductCategoryField row. The measured column carried ProductCategory|tc_content|tcMedia, which is not a field on any host: the real system name is tcMediaSet. A typed name that resolves to nothing is silent - no exception, no dw-error, correct row counts everywhere.

fieldDisplayGroupsBound.scopeNote: tc_specs spans four categories (tc_commerce, tc_content, tc_product_structure, tc_users) and a product renders only the fields it carries a value for, so a product whose values all sit in one category shows that category's fields and no others. A data layer that wants the band fuller spreads values across the categories the group spans; it does not shorten the group. The same four categories are the four PIM data models sample-data 5.0.0 attaches under its TCSHOP-PIM shop, and each one's completion rule names exactly the seven fields of its category - so the spec table a product renders and the completeness score it carries are computed from the same set.

assetCategoriesBound.note: CONSUMER PREREQUISITE (Foundry #1196). Three PDP paragraphs this surface ships bind product ASSET CATEGORIES by system name through their ImageAssets field. The categories themselves are catalogue-side configuration and NO layer in a base-swift composition ships them, so on a content-free build the PDP gallery and both document tables resolve nothing and render empty behind an HTTP 200. A tool-first build has to discover the dependency by reading paragraph settings, which is the defect this note closes.

requiredRows.purpose: The PDP Documents table and its teaser (Swift-v2_ProductMediaTable).

assetCategoriesBound.satisfiedBy: layers/sample-data merge/_sql/EcomDetailsGroup/100110.yml (Images) + 100111.yml (Manuals). Any edition with sampleData true - swift-demo, headless-demo, dap-portal - already meets this prerequisite and needs no consumer action. base-swift does NOT, by design.
assetCategoriesBound.whyNotShippedByThisLayer: Not a table-safety problem: EcomDetailsGroup is NOT a heap (its _meta.yml declares keyColumns EcomDetailsGroupId, an identity PRIMARY KEY), so the Serializer truncate-on-heap defect (Truvio.Commerce.Serializer #21) does not apply and the table would carry rows safely. The blockers are ownership and composition. (1) sample-data already ships these two exact rows, and the merge gate's cross-layer collision guard (Validate-Distribution.ps1 check 6) FAILs when two ACTIVE layers ship the same _sql/<Table>/<key>.yml - a real last-writer-wins hazard, not a formality. (2) Moving them here instead is worse: headless-demo composes sample-data WITHOUT surface-swift, and 374 sample-data EcomDetails rows point at EcomDetailsGroupId 100110/100111, so the move would orphan every one of them on that edition. base cannot carry them either - it is FRAMEWORK-ONLY by contract (zero catalog) since the Swift 2.4 base split, and asset categories are catalogue-side configuration.

consumerObligation.whenRequired: Any composition that takes surface-swift WITHOUT sample-data - base-swift above all - must create the two categories before a PDP can render assets.
consumerObligation.verb: Management API AssetCategorySave. Dynamicweb.MCP 0.4.4 publishes NO tool for product asset categories (get_product_asset_categories reads them; nothing writes one), which is the other half of Foundry #1196; ProductItemAdd is the matching verb for the BOM items Swift-v2_ProductBom needs.
consumerObligation.matchedBy: System name, not id. The paragraphs name 'Images' and 'Manuals' as strings, so a consumer's own ids are fine as long as the system names match exactly, case included.
consumerObligation.verify: On a build with a product carrying a Manuals asset, the PDP Documents table renders rows with no SQL and no undocumented setup.

assetCategoriesBound.source: Foundry #1196 (foundry-base arm agent 2, 2026-09-13: categories Images id 7, Manuals id 8 on a base-swift build).
